summary: Configured OPNsense node1 to route between lan-a (10.60.1.0/24, opt1/vtnet1) and lan-b (10.60.2.0/24, opt2/vtnet2). Added static addressing on node2 (10.60.1.11) and node3 (10.60.2.12) with routes via node1, firewall pass rules on both new interfaces, and a manual/hybrid outbound NAT rule that SNATs traffic sourced from 10.60.1.0/24 egressing via opt2 to node1's lan-b address (10.60.2.1). Verified node2->node3 connections are observed by node3 as arriving from 10.60.2.1 (node1), while node3->node2 connections keep node3's real address. Restarted all three nodes one at a time (OPNsense native reboot, systemctl reboot for RHEL nodes), proved changed boot identity on each (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3), and re-verified the NAT/routing behavior and connectivity after each restart, plus a final full end-to-end re-test after all three nodes were rebooted.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense), node2/node3 (RHEL10) network topology and interfaces
Read OPNsense filter.inc/SNatRule.php source to determine correct config.xml schema for outbound NAT rules

Edited node1 /conf/config.xml: added opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces, pass rules for both, switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode with SNAT rule for 10.60.1.0/24 -> opt2 interface address
Applied config via configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload
Configured node2 enp8s0 (10.60.1.11/24) and node3 enp8s0 (10.60.2.12/24) via nmcli with static routes to the opposite lan via node1
Verified via Python TCP client/server that node2->node3 connections appear sourced from 10.60.2.1 and node3->node2 connections keep original 10.60.2.12 source
Captured pre-restart boot identity and health evidence on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via /usr/local/etc/rc.reboot, node2 and node3 via systemctl reboot, one at a time, waiting for each to recover before proceeding
Verified changed boot identity (kern.boottime for node1, boot_id for node2/node3) and re-verified interfaces/routes/NAT/connectivity/mapping behavior after each restart
Ran a final full mapping verification across all three nodes after all restarts completed
Cleaned up temporary firewalld ports opened for testing

evidence.requirement: node2 on lan-a to node3 on lan-b connections appear to node3 as originating from a chosen address on node1
evidence.summary: node2 python client shows its own local addr as 10.60.1.11, but node3's listening server logged the incoming connection as ('10.60.2.1', ...) -- node1's lan-b (opt2) address

evidence.requirement: connections in the other direction (node3 -> node2) keep their original source address (no NAT)
evidence.summary: node3 python client used its real address 10.60.2.12 to connect to node2, and node2's server observed the connection as ('10.60.2.12', ...) -- unNATed

evidence.requirement: NAT/routing config in OPNsense config.xml and applied pf ruleset
evidence.summary: config.xml updated with opt1/opt2 interfaces and hybrid-mode SNAT rule; interfaces came up with correct IPs; filter reload succeeded; pfctl -s nat shows 'nat on vtnet2 inet from 10.60.1.0/24 to any -> (vtnet2:0)'; pfctl -s rules shows pass rules on vtnet1/vtnet2
kern.boottime = Sat Sep 5 17:04:34 2026; opt1/opt2 interfaces up with correct IPs; NAT rule present

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: rc.reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec timed out (node down); later exec succeeded with kern.boottime = 17:10:32 2026, a later boot time proving restart

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of NAT/routing/filter state and functional mapping
evidence.summary: post-reboot ifconfig/pfctl show opt1/opt2 IPs, SNAT rule, and pass rules intact; live test connection from node2 observed by node3 as arriving from 10.60.2.1
boot_id b17495e3-5cde-49a9-b0d1-ab2e1461726a captured with enp8s0 configured at 10.60.1.11/24

boot_id 19062a82-6390-435d-a09f-4dba1593d529 captured with enp8s0 configured at 10.60.2.12/24

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; subsequent exec timed out; later exec returned new boot_id 92f36b90-aa38-46bc-a568-5821a89f0045 (changed from baseline); post-reboot ip addr/route and ping to node2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: final end-to-end verification of NAT mapping after all three nodes restarted
